program_terms.applies_to: main applicant and family members
program_terms.quote: An investment residence permit shall be issued to an alien who has made at least GEL 300,000 worth of investment in Georgia
program_terms.notes: Consolidated English version of 20 Mar 2015 restating the 2014 law. Under art. 16(3) this permit is granted with the right of permanent residence. Dates as for the same rule from the 2014 text: in force 1 Sep 2014 (the English versions misprint art. 74 as 1 January 2014); replaced by USD 300,000 from 5 Jun 2019 (2019-05 version).

program_terms.applies_to: residence permit applications and extensions (all types, incl. the investment residence permit), from submission of all required documents
program_terms.quote: The period for considering an application for obtaining a residence permit and for extending its validity period shall not exceed 30 days from the submission of all the required documents to the Agency.
program_terms.notes: As in the consolidated version of 20 Mar 2015; the date this provision took effect is not printed beside it (valid_from left empty). By the 2026 version the period is left to a government ordinance.

program_terms.applies_to: D5 immigration visa: owner of non-agricultural real property and family members; market value above the amount (in laris), set by a certified assessor
program_terms.quote: D5 – to individuals who, under the procedure established by the legislation of Georgia, have the right of ownership of real property within the territory of Georgia (other than agricultural land) with its market value exceeding USD 35 000 equivalent in laris, and their family members.
program_terms.notes: The D5 immigration visa, added by Law No 3602 (published 15.5.2015), uses the same threshold as the short-term residence permit (art. 15(j)). Replaced by USD 100,000 in the 2019-05 version (from 5 Jun 2019, as for the permit).

program_terms.applies_to: long-term visa issued with a D5 immigration visa (multiple entry; validity and duration of stay)
program_terms.quote: A long-term visa with one year validity period shall be issued only when a D5 immigration visa is granted.
program_terms.notes: Other long-term visas: 90 calendar days. Added by Law No 3602 (history note on the article).

program_terms.applies_to: D5 immigration visa: decision after the visa application is submitted
program_terms.quote: The decision to issue a D5 immigration visa shall be made within 10 calendar days after an appropriate visa application is submitted.
program_terms.notes: Other D-category visas: 30 calendar days.

program_terms.applies_to: short-term residence permit for real-property owners (art. 15(j)); terminates when ownership ends
program_terms.quote: A short-term residence permit provided for in Article 15(j) of this Law may be issued to an alien for one year period.
program_terms.notes: Extended on the same conditions without a new valuation if ownership continues (art. 16(4)).

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant and family members
program_terms.quote: An investment residence permit shall be issued to an alien who has made at least GEL 300,000 worth of investment in Georgia
program_terms.notes: Restated in the consolidated version of 8 May 2015; investment permit carries the right of permanent residence (art. 16(3)).

program_terms.applies_to: residence permit applications and extensions (all types, incl. investment and property-owner permits), from submission of all required documents
program_terms.quote: The period for considering an application for obtaining a residence permit and for extending its validity period shall not exceed 30 days from the submission of all the required documents to the Agency.
program_terms.notes: As in the consolidated version of 8 May 2015; date the provision took effect not printed beside it.

program_terms.applies_to: investment residence permit on the investment basis: annual turnover of the entrepreneurial activity in the first year (in GEL equivalent); without proof the permit terminates
program_terms.location: PDF p. 10, Article 16(1)(e); also Article 15(k) and Article 21(12)
program_terms.quote: The validity of an investment residence permit shall be terminated if an alien has no proof of the annual turnover of at least USD 50 000 equivalent in GEL during the first year of the entrepreneurial activities
program_terms.notes: Holder must submit Revenue Service turnover information annually (art. 16(1)(e)). Introduced by Law No 4741 of 2019 per the programme notes; the version date the provision took effect is not printed beside it (history notes list Laws 3602 and 4741).

program_terms.applies_to: investment residence permit on the investment basis: annual turnover in the second year (in GEL equivalent)
program_terms.location: PDF p. 10, Article 16(1)(e); also Article 15(k) and Article 21(12)
program_terms.quote: the annual turnover of at least USD 100 000 equivalent in GEL during the second year
program_terms.notes: Same rule as the first-year threshold; also the condition for the unlimited permit (art. 15(k)).

program_terms.applies_to: investment residence permit on the investment basis: annual turnover in each of the third, fourth and fifth years (in GEL equivalent)
program_terms.location: PDF p. 10, Article 16(1)(e); also Article 15(k) and Article 21(12)
program_terms.quote: the turnover of at least USD 120 000 equivalent in GEL during the third, fourth and fifth years
program_terms.notes: Fifth-year turnover of at least USD 120,000 must be shown when applying for the unlimited permit before the 5-year permit expires (art. 16(5)).

program_terms.applies_to: D5 immigration visa: owner of non-agricultural real property, spouse and children; market value above the amount (in GEL), set by a certified assessor
program_terms.quote: D5 category – to an individual who, under the procedure established by the legislation of Georgia, has the right of ownership of real property within the territory of Georgia (other than agricultural land) with its market value exceeding USD 150 000 equivalent in GEL
program_terms.notes: Same threshold as the short-term residence permit (art. 15(j)); raised to USD 150,000 by Law No 863 of 26 June 2025 per the programme notes.

program_terms.applies_to: long-term visa issued with a D5 (or D6) immigration visa (multiple entry; validity and duration of stay)
program_terms.quote: A long-term visa with one-year validity period shall be issued when a D5 and D6 category immigration visas are granted.
program_terms.notes: Other long-term visas: 90 calendar days.

program_terms.applies_to: D5 immigration visa: decision after the visa application is submitted
program_terms.quote: The decision to issue a D5 category immigration visa shall be made within 10 calendar days after an appropriate visa application is submitted.
program_terms.notes: Other D-category visas: 30 calendar days.

program_terms.quote: გრძელვადიანი ვიზა 1 წლის მოქმედების ვადით გაიცემა მხოლოდ D5 კატეგორიის საიმიგრაციო ვიზის გაცემის შემთხვევაში

program_terms.applies_to: temporary residence permit holders (all grounds, incl. art. 45 company owners): permit revoked if the alien leaves to live, or lives, abroad longer than this
program_terms.quote: užsienietis išvyksta gyventi arba gyvena užsienio valstybėje ilgiau negu 6 mėnesius;
program_terms.notes: General ground for revoking any temporary residence permit; applies to the art. 45 permit. In force 2004-04-30 (e-seimas record).

program_terms.applies_to: holder of a temporary residence permit (any ground) who has lived in Lithuania without interruption for the last 5 years
program_terms.quote: jis pragyveno Lietuvos Respublikoje be pertraukos pastaruosius 5 metus ir turėjo leidimą laikinai gyventi;
program_terms.notes: General route to permanent residence, not specific to company owners; the period can be cut by one year for those who pass the state-language exam (art. 53(6)). The permanent residence permit is issued for 5 years and then replaced (art. 53(4)).

program_terms.applies_to: temporary residence permit applications (all grounds, incl. art. 54 property owners), from submission of a complete application
program_terms.quote: 0 zahtjevu za izdavanje dozvole za privremeni boravak odluouje se u roku od 40 dana od dana predaje urednog zahtjeva.
program_terms.notes: General rule for temporary residence permits. Quote as in the OCR text ("0" for "O", "odluouje" for "odlučuje"). valid_from is the date the law applies from (art. 145), as for the other rules from this law.

program_terms.applies_to: extension of a temporary residence permit (all grounds, incl. art. 54); new permit valid up to one year
program_terms.quote: najkasnije u roku od 30 dana prije isteka roka va2enja dozvole za privremeni boravak.
program_terms.notes: General rule for temporary residence permits (OCR "va2enja" for "važenja").

program_terms.applies_to: general route: 5 years of continuous lawful temporary residence; time spent on temporary residence for use of real property owned in Montenegro is NOT counted
program_terms.quote: zahtjeva za izdavanje dozvole zakonito boravio u Crnoj God neprekidno pet godina na osnovu odobrenog privremenog boravka
program_terms.notes: The same article excludes from the five years time spent on "privremenom boravku radi raspolaganja pravom na nepokretnosti koje stranac posjeduje u Crnoj Gori" (art. 82(5)(2)): property-based residence does not lead to permanent residence. Absences of up to ten months in total, or six months at once, in the five years do not break continuity.

program_terms.applies_to: long-stay visa (visa D) for a foreigner intending to stay more than 90 days, for (among other purposes) the use and disposal of rights to real property owned in Montenegro; requires proof of ownership and of funds for subsistence, accommodation, health insurance and return
program_terms.location: PDF p. 3, art. 8 (new art. 18(1)) and art. 18 para. on real property
program_terms.quote: duze od 90 dana, ali ne duze od 180 dana u vremenskom periodu od jedne godine
program_terms.notes: New art. 18 lists "koriscenja i raspolaganja pravom na nepokretnosti koju posjeduje u Crnoj Gori" among the purposes of the D visa, and a later paragraph sets the proof required for property owners. The amending law enters into force on the eighth day after publication in the Official Gazette (publication not stored), so valid_from is left empty.

program_terms.applies_to: extension of a temporary residence permit (all grounds, incl. property owners): application no earlier than 60 days before expiry; property owners must also prove taxes paid during the permit
program_terms.location: PDF p. 14, art. 31 (amending art. 64(1) and adding a paragraph on real property)
program_terms.quote: U clanu 64 stav 1 poslije rijeci „boravka,“ dodaju se rijeci: „najranije u roku od 60, a“.
program_terms.notes: The amendment inserts an earliest filing date before the existing latest date in art. 64(1) of the 2018 law (not printed in full here). The new paragraph requires, for extending a property-based permit, proof of tax obligations met while the permit lasted. Entry into force: eighth day after publication (not stored).

program_terms.applies_to: owner of a plot of land for building in an ITC and first-degree relatives: multiple-entry investor visa, issued for two years at a time until the building is complete
program_terms.quote: وتمنح تأشيرة مستثمر برحلات متعددة بواقع سنتين لكل مرة لمالك قطعة الأرض المعدة للبناء ولأقاربه من الدرجة الأولى وذلك حتى اكتمال البناء
program_terms.notes: Plot owners get an investor visa rather than residence; built-unit owners get the 2-year residence already recorded. valid_from: the decision applies from the day after publication (art. 3) in Official Gazette No 848 of 1 Oct 2007.

program_terms.currency: years from registration of the land
program_terms.applies_to: owner of a plot of land in an ITC: must build and finish it (or reach the completed-unit stage, or use it for its purpose) within this period
program_terms.quote: وذلك كله خلال مدة لا تتجاوز أربع سنوات من تاريخ تسجيل الأرض باسمه في السجل العقاري
program_terms.notes: Until then the plot may only be mortgaged to finance building (art. 15). valid_from: the decision applies from the day after publication (art. 3) in Official Gazette No 848 of 1 Oct 2007.

program_terms.applies_to: owner of a plot of land in an ITC: extension of the 4-year building period, on the Ministry of Tourism's recommendation, requested before the original period ends
program_terms.quote: تحدد المدة الإضافية التي يجوز منحها للمالك بسنتين على الأكثر
program_terms.notes: Starts the day after the four years end (art. 13). valid_from: the decision applies from the day after publication (art. 3) in Official Gazette No 848 of 1 Oct 2007.

program_terms.applies_to: owner (المالك) who violates the regulations or agreements and does not remove the violation after warning: maximum fine, set by the gravity of the violation
program_terms.quote: على ألا تتجاوز خمسين ألف ريال عماني للمطور وخمسة آلاف ريال عماني للمالك
program_terms.notes: Imposed by the Minister, without prejudice to other penalties. valid_from: the decision applies from the day after publication (art. 3) in Official Gazette No 848 of 1 Oct 2007.

program_terms.applies_to: developer (المطور) of an ITC who violates the regulations or agreements and does not remove the violation after warning: maximum fine
program_terms.quote: على ألا تتجاوز خمسين ألف ريال عماني للمطور وخمسة آلاف ريال عماني للمالك
program_terms.notes: Fine on the developer, not the investor; recorded because it is part of the programme's rules. valid_from: the decision applies from the day after publication (art. 3) in Official Gazette No 848 of 1 Oct 2007.

program_terms.applies_to: owner convicted by final judgment of a crime against honour or trust, or subject to a final deportation decision: period to dispose of the property through an agent before it is sold at public auction
program_terms.quote: فإن ذلك لا يخل بحقه في التصرف في العقار خلال سنة بمعرفة من يوكله في ذلك

Home Affairs BP0068 workbook: Migration Program (and Child) outcomes 2015-16 to 2024-25 as a pivot table over a 622,425-record cache with fields programme year, visa program/category/type/sub-type/subclass, citizenship country, gender, applicant type, age group, client location, occupation (five levels) and intended residence. The visible sheet shows only Migration Program totals by category (Family, Skilled, Special Eligibility, Child), which are out of scope. In scope: the Business Innovation and Investment visa type and its streams, and the legacy investor subclasses 165 and 893. Extracted (by summing the pivot cache with the filters named in each location, as the earlier rows do): for the Significant Investor, Significant Investor Extension, Investor and Premium Investor streams, subclasses 165 and 893, and the BIIP visa type as a whole, every year with records: total, primary, secondary, by citizenship country (all, primary, secondary), by gender, by intended state, by age group, by client location and by visa subclass; for the other BIIP sub-types (Business Innovation, Business Innovation Extension, Entrepreneur, Significant Business History, Venture Capital Entrepreneur, Business Skills, State/Territory Sponsored Business Skills): total, primary and secondary per year. Stream (sub-type) detail exists only from 2017-18; 2015-16 and 2016-17 BIIP grants sit under Business Skills sub-types. Every split adds up to its total (checked). Sums below 5 are stored as ranges 0-4 because the data is masked (decision 3); 10 sums that come out negative are held back. Zero cells are not recorded. Four 188 records under Global Talent (Independent) in 2021-22 are outside the BIIP visa type and not taken. Occupation is "Not Specified" for all investor-stream primaries (not extracted). This pass (extract-partials-p4-2026-10-11) re-checked the scope: the other BIIP sub-types (Business Innovation, its extension, Entrepreneur, Significant Business History, Venture Capital Entrepreneur, Business Skills) rest on running or funding a business, not a personal minimum investment, so only their totals (already in) are kept as context (decision 15); no rows added.

No minimum property value in the law. Earlier: 1 rule and 2 events. Law amending Montenegro's Law on Foreigners, adopted 31 Dec 2025 (promulgation decree and text, 41 pp.; the stored file repeats the text twice): new D-visa article (stays of 90-180 days a year, incl. for property owners, with proof of ownership and funds), digital nomad residence (out of scope), EUR 150,000 minimum real-estate transfer-tax base for property-based residence with EU/EEA/Swiss exemption (art. 24), extension rules (earliest 60 days before expiry; property owners prove taxes paid, art. 31), work permits incl. EUR 5,000 annual taxes for owner-directors (employment route, out of scope), fines, transitional rule art. 217b (renewals of property permits issued before entry into force are decided under the old law, i.e. without the EUR 150,000 test), entry into force on the eighth day after publication (publication not stored). Earlier: EUR 150,000 rule and adoption event. This pass added 2 rules: D-visa stay limit for property owners and the 60-day earliest renewal filing.

Government of Montenegro bill for a Law on Foreigners (10 Sep 2014, 126 pp.): draft law text, explanatory memorandum (novelties incl. art. 54 residence for use of real property of a certain value, PDF p. 51), statement that no extra budget funds are needed, and an EU-law concordance table. The draft art. 54 (1-year permit; value conditions left to a government regulation) and the permanent-residence exclusion match the adopted law (mne-skupstina-aliens-law-2014), where they are recorded as rules; a bill is not in force, so its draft provisions are not recorded as rules. The memorandum's statement is already an event. No numbers about the programme. Re-read in this pass; no rows added.

Oman Ministerial Decision 191/2007 (Ministry of Housing, 19 Sep 2007; Official Gazette 848, 1 Oct 2007; in force the next day) issuing the executive regulations of the Integrated Tourism Complexes (ITC) ownership system (Royal Decree 12/2006), as published on qanoon.om: definitions; who may own (Omanis and non-Omanis); ITC licensing conditions (200,000 m2 minimum, 30% built-up ratio, 50% non-tourism cap, 20 km from borders: developer conditions, out of scope); registration and the developer's land share (+6% a year, out of scope); plot owners must build within 4 years (+ up to 2); inheritance and estate management (fee up to 10% of rent, out of scope); forced sale within 1 year after conviction or deportation; residence for built-unit owners and first-degree relatives (granted within 7 working days; 2 years, renewed automatically for six years) and a 2-year multiple-entry investor visa for plot owners; residence for two representatives of a company owner; continued residence for heirs; fines up to OMR 50,000 (developer) and OMR 5,000 (owner). Earlier: 2 rules and 1 event. This pass added 6 rules: plot owners' investor visa (2 years per issue), 4-year building deadline and 2-year maximum extension, maximum fines for owners and developers, 1-year forced-sale period. The 2022 amendments (MD 109/2022) are a separate instrument not stored with this source (lead, not a gap in this document).

Turkey Law 6458 on Foreigners and International Protection, consolidated text (mevzuat.gov.tr, 48 pp.): entry, visas, residence permits (art. 30-49) incl. short-term residence for owners of real property (art. 31(1)(b)) and for investors in the scope and amount set by the President (art. 31(1)(j), added 2016), permit durations (2 years; 5 years for investors), the Ministry setting the qualifying property value (art. 31(6), added 2024), long-term permit after 8 years, absence rule; international protection, administration (out of scope); entry into force (art. 125) and a list of amending acts with in-force dates. The law prints no amounts: the property value and investment amount are set by the Ministry and the President (instruments not stored). This pass proposed two programmes (tur-property-residence, tur-investor-residence) and added 8 rules (permit durations, unset property value and investment amount, 8-year long-term permit and absence rule for each) and 3 events (2014 entry into force, 2016 investor ground, 2024 ministerial property value).

Immigration Act 13 of 2002 as gazetted (Government Gazette 23478, 31 May 2002; scanned, 43 pp., OCR text): definitions, visas and temporary residence permits incl. the business permit (s. 15: prescribed financial or capital contribution, accountant's certification renewed within 24 months and every two years, waiver for national-interest businesses), permanent residence incl. s. 27(c) for business investors (certification renewed within two years and three years thereafter or the permit lapses) and s. 27(f) financially independent (net worth, out of scope), offences, commencement by proclamation (s. 55). No amounts in the Act (contribution prescribed by regulation). Earlier: the publication event. This pass added 4 rules (the certification renewal periods for the business permit and s. 27(c) permanent residence), after checking the figures against a fresh OCR of the page images (PDF pp. 16 and 22).

South African Embassy Copenhagen (DIRCO) checklist "Application for a Business Visa" (6 pp.; the stored text repeats once): legal basis (s. 15 as amended, excluded sectors under s. 15(1A)), documents, requirements for a new business (R5,000,000 cash, or cash plus new machinery/equipment, from abroad; 60% South African staff undertaking; registrations; dti recommendation) and for an established business (same amounts available or already invested; proof of 60% staff; registrations; financial statements and proof of investment), police, medical and radiological reports, family documents, fee DKK 882, notes (staff proof within 12 months; visa up to three years; proof of investment within 24 months and every two years; waiver for national-interest businesses; multiple entry). Earlier: R5,000,000 new-business cash rule. This pass added 7 rules: the cash-plus-equipment alternative and the two established-business amounts, the 60% staff requirement, the DKK 882 fee, 3-year maximum validity and the investment-proof intervals.

gov.za document page for the Immigration Act 13 of 2002: purpose, related acts, commencement dates (ss. 7 and 52 on 20 Feb 2003; s. 4 on 26 Feb 2003; all other sections except s. 37 on 12 Mar 2003, Gazette 24951 of 20 Feb 2003), link to the consolidated text on SAFLII, and the list of amending acts (Immigration Amendment Acts 19 of 2004, 3 of 2007, 13 of 2011, 8 of 2016; and three other acts on corruption, sexual offences and trafficking, not about the investor route). Earlier: the 12 Mar 2003 commencement event. This pass added 4 events (one per Immigration Amendment Act, year precision; the page does not say what each changed). The partial commencements of ss. 4, 7 and 52 are not about the business route (not recorded).

Zambia Development Agency Act No 11 of 2006 (assented 12 May 2006; scanned, 45 pp., OCR text that repeats the Act twice): the Agency and Board, investment promotion, licences/permits/certificates of registration for business enterprises (valid 10 years; these are ZDA investment licences, not residence permits), incentives (USD 500,000 in a priority sector for tax and customs incentives, USD 10 million for major-investment incentives, 5-year validity: tax incentives, out of scope under METHODOLOGY 15), land, s. 65 immigration (investor of at least USD 250,000 employing at least 200 persons is entitled to a self-employment or residence permit; Board help with up to five expatriate work permits), micro and small enterprises, offences. Earlier: USD 250,000 rule and the legal event. This pass added 2 rules: the 200-employee minimum (confirmed against two fresh OCR readings of the page image) and the up-to-five expatriate work permits. Commencement by statutory instrument (not stored).
